newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Court orders ballot on Australia gold dispute.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Court orders ballot on Australia gold dispute.

text.p: The long-running legal dispute over ownership of one of Australia's most sought after gold mining tenements on Friday moved a step closer to being finally resolved when the Western Australian Supreme Court ordered that a ballot be held to resolve who has priority.

The Full Court of Western Australia also ordered that only two of the four parties disputing ownership of the tenement - over a 15 km patch of ground directly opposite the rich Bronzewing gold mine - be eligible to take part in the ballot.
However, legal sources stressed the ballot may still not finally resolve the dispute because of the over-riding discretionary powers of the Minister for Mines which entitle him to have the final say.
The 2-1 majority decision of the Full Court of the Supreme Court is the latest chapter in a dispute dating back to 15 October, 1992.
On that day four parties lodged a total of eight applications for an exploration licence over the land, at the Leonora Mining Registry within 51 seconds of the Registry opening for business.

Subsequently the Mining Warden determined that, for the purposes of the Mining Act 1978, the four applicants had complied with the requirements of the Act "at the same time" and a ballot should held to resolve who had priority.
Two of the applicants appealed the ballot decision but the Supreme Court decided, in a judgement handed down in 1994, that it didn't have jurisdiction to intervene.
This decision was overturned, however, on appeal to the High Court. The case was referred back to the Supreme Court for hearing and its decision was handed down on Friday.

The two parties that the Supreme Court determined would now take part in the ballot are prospector Mark Creasy and a private company - Hot Holdings Pty Ltd - which has an agreement with the listed gold miner Audax Resources NL in relation to 80 percent of its interest.
